design: Two H100 allocations; opposite budget order on each allocation; three randomized repeats per budget per GPU; identical prompts and case order within a GPU pair.
aggregate_metric: Sum of output tokens divided by concurrent wave wall seconds.
stream_metric: Output tokens after first event divided by time from first event to final event.
comparison_metric: Geometric mean of six paired 8192/4096 wave ratios; reported percent change.
cache_policy: Unique request salts; no cross-request prefix reuse.
limitations: Two GPUs and six paired waves per shape provide descriptive replication, not a production confidence guarantee.
Code/docs are repository text; records and conversations are synthetic, not production traffic.
Batch arrivals, without public HTTP routing or billing.
No nonzero trained LoRA or multimodal throughput qualification.
Existing hosted FP8 checkpoint mapping is not revision-pinned.
Forced-length cases ignore EOS; natural-EOS cases analyzed separately.
Every EOS-enabled case reached its 512-token cap. These are not observed natural-length completion tests.
Main-data slow waves are retained: docs-512-c32 aggregate -3.1%, conversation-4096-c8 -1.3%. Only the short-document case received a focused follow-up.
The focused run used a fixed budget order; its 20 pairs are descriptive and do not provide an independent crossover.
Token-output hashes did not match across paired budget runs (0/3880). This benchmark measures performance and completion, not semantic quality or output equivalence.
focused_design: 20 paired docs-512-c32 waves, one additional H100 allocation, fixed 4096 then 8192 order. Separate follow-up; not pooled with main data.
